Hi all

we're hosting a statlib office hour. Here's what we plan to discuss

  1. AI is getting better at writing Lean — takeaways from the FLT project and TauCeti. What does this mean for how we build statlib? We are proposing the vision should be a human-interactable repo that hold community trust

  2. Where the real bottleneck is — as AI getting better at both math and coding, the core digest will probably be a design doc including both math and code. We propose writing design docs in markdown from the start, so we can challenge each other on definitions, statements, interfaces, and scope before any Lean is written. We'd also like to propose use less AI and keep sentence short and precise, so humans are really collaborating with humans. A proposed template can be found in [link]

  3. A proposed workflow: roadmap markdown → review → implementation → CI checks → AI review → human review → merge. For the AI review, we are thinking about the harness in (rubrics at TauCeti project [link] ).

Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fcKLQ00Eq0v76Dbc9JIhAESE51_ilgCqyzAyNU_WyHY/edit?usp=sharing

Any comments and welcome !

My 2 pence. I think it’d be good to understand what formalisation of stats is for; I don’t think everyone has the same goals - eg prediction, inference, data exploration. For some goals, such as getting the absolutely best bounds with the absolutely best constants, and knowing that they are true, because a medical discovery depends on it, it is somewhat secondary in my opinion how beautiful the code is or whether it was done by AI. For others, the structure of the proof matters because it captures an important way of thinking. I don’t have a very coherent general position on the whole thing, I should probably be quiet :)

Hi Patrick, I agree that it would be amazing to attach a formalization for an uncertainty quantification given by an algorithm. Pretty difficult though because that will depend on a modelling assumption, and the biggest uncertainty is how well that model approximates reality. What might help is many AI agents --- AI statisticians --- that can use formal tools (lean, python, other software) and reason about a real-world scenario, comparing different decisions under different models.
